A causal-discovery method specification

Source: R/cd-method.R
cd_method.Rd

Bundles the metadata that drives selection – family, language, native output type, cost, and assumptions – with the adapter that runs a back-end algorithm on a data matrix and returns its estimate in the shared amat.cpdag convention. The available predicate reports whether the back-end can run in the current session, so a method whose package or Python module is absent is skipped rather than failing.

Usage

cd_method(
  id = character(0),
  name = "",
  family = "constraint",
  language = "R",
  output = "cpdag",
  citation = "",
  cost = "fast",
  assumptions = "",
  accepts = "data",
  available = function() NULL,
  run = function() NULL
)

Arguments

id

A single string identifying the method; this is the value passed to method = in cd_discover().

name

A single string giving the human-readable method name.

family

A single string naming the algorithm family, one of "constraint", "score", "functional", "continuous_optim", "hybrid", or "density".

language

A single string, "R" or "Python".

output

A single string giving the native output type, one of "dag", "cpdag", or "pag".

citation

A single string citing the method's source.

cost

A single string giving the rough computational cost, one of "fast", "medium", "slow", or "very_slow".

assumptions

A single string describing the method's modelling assumptions.

accepts

A single string naming the input the method's run consumes, "data" (the default; a numeric observation matrix) or "suffstat" (a sufficient statistic, the list list(C, n) of a correlation matrix and its sample size). A "suffstat" method can still be called on a data matrix – cd_discover() reduces the data to its sufficient statistic first.

available

A function of no arguments returning a single logical: can the method run in the current session?

run

A function taking the method's input (a numeric data matrix, or a list(C, n) sufficient statistic when accepts = "suffstat") and returning a list with elements amat (the estimate in amat.cpdag convention, or NULL), runtime_s, and status.

Value

An S7 object of class cd_method.

See also

Other registry: list_methods(), register_method()

Examples

cd_method(
  id = "demo", name = "Demo", family = "constraint",
  available = function() TRUE,
  run = function(data) list(amat = NULL, runtime_s = 0, status = "ok")
)
#> <cd_method 'demo'>: Demo [constraint, R]
#>   output     : cpdag
#>   cost       : fast
#>   available  : yes
